text.p: Rubbermaid Inc. Wednesday reported lower earnings for the latest quarter, saying its results were squeezed by the continued rise in plastic resin prices and lagging sales.

The company said it earned $46.1 million or 31 cents a share in the third quarter, down from year-ago earnings of $50.2 million or 32 cents a share. Sales dropped to $632.7 million from $641.5 million.

"Our results reflect lagging sales of large outdoor juvenile products and the effects of continuing sharp increases in plastic resin costs over past months," said Wolfgang Schmitt, chairman and chief executive officer.
"These factors have directly offset the ongoing fundamental improvements being made throughout our business," he said.
Rubbermaid's second-quarter earnings were also hurt by higher plastic resin costs.
The company said its acquisition of Graco Children's Products Inc., a maker of infant furniture, will boost its growth starting next year.
Early this month, Rubbermaid paid $320 million for Graco, which will complement the firm's existing products for children, such as its Little Tikes toys, furniture and play equipment.
Rubbermaid's stock was off 12.5 cents at $24.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.
